B.Cu GND pour is ONE island of 452.576 mm2 with EXACTLY TWO interior voids: 14.369 mm2 centred (34.585,24.812) bbox 3.900x3.901 = J1.1 roundrect + 0.80 mm rule (exact 14.35); 8.064 mm2 centred (40.135,24.812) bbox 3.200x3.201 = C1.2 pad + 0.80 mm (exact 8.042). headline_verified.claim: RL 32.17 dB at the +5% resistance corner on 7.21 nH = 1.13 ohm vs a 12.07 ohm / 76.9 nH threshold
headline_verified.independent: R_eff = R + X^2/R; X(7.21 nH, 25 MHz) = 1.1325 ohm; R_eff(52.5) = 52.5244; |G| = 0.024623; RL = 32.17 dB. Threshold X at R=52.5 for R_eff <= 55.2757 is 12.072 ohm = 76.9 nH; margin 10.66x. Method cross-checked against the run's own ngspice: my closed form gives 25.34 dB at R=52.5/X=13.0, reff_limit.cir measures s_b_x130 = -25.3366.

violations.msg: Port shunt-capacitance budget is stale by ~3x: blocks.md s4.3 budgets 1.30 pF from a 3.55 mm x 1.1 mm launch, but the as-built launch is 15.065 mm flaring to 7.34 mm plus a 5.0 x 7.0 mm lap pad. Recomputed from the board stackup (h=1.53, er=4.5) with impedance.microstrip_z0: tracks 2.27 pF + lap pad 1.50 pF + J1.1 pad 0.25 pF + 0.60 pF internal = ~4.7 pF on the net, ~2.0 pF port-side. Nulling 7.21 nH needs 2.883 pF total and C1's low stop is 1.0 pF, so the trimmer will sit AT or PAST its stop with no downward authority. Return loss is safe (bounding case, all 4.7 pF at the port: 39.1 dB at R=50, 31.2 dB at +5% corner, vs a 26 dB spec) but README.md:82-83 'authority in both directions' is probably false on the bench, and decision 58 justifies the entire flare-stopping choice by preserving that two-sided null. Re-derive blocks.md s4.3 against the as-built geometry and soften the README claim; no copper change warranted.

The sim gate validates a trimmer that is not on the BOM: all four benches set .param cmax=35e-12 (tuning_authority.cir:38, s11_band.cir:49, s11_corners.cir:30) but the delivered Johanson 5602 is 1-30 pF. With cpad=1.3p that models 2.3-36.3 pF against a real 2.3-31.3 pF. Consequences: lnull_hi_nh=99.64 / xnull_hi_ohm=15.65 / lnull_span_nh=93.89 are wrong for the shipped part (correct: 83.65 nH / 13.14 ohm / 77.90 nH, which is what the README states - so README and sim disagree and only the README is right), and README.md:81-82 '>= 26 dB is actually held from 0 nH to ~103 nH' is inherited from the stale bench - with the real 31.3 pF maximum the crossing is at 99.0 nH. cmin=1e-12 is correct for the 5602 and the board lives at the low stop, so there is no board risk, but 'sim PASS, 4 benches / 116 bounds' does not cover C1's high stop. Re-run with cmax=30e-12.

README.md:108-110 states that a 0.1 uH 'non-inductive' power resistor gives '26.6 dB at best and 25.5 dB with a +5 % part'. At R=52.5 and X=15.708 ohm the correct figure is R_eff=57.200, |G|=0.06716, RL=23.46 dB - not 25.5 dB. (The 26.55 dB at R=50 is correct.) The argument is unaffected and in fact strengthened; the number is wrong by 2 dB.

README.md:80-81 claims the trimmer's low-stop over-correction is 'worth under 0.4 % reflection'. At L=0 with the 2.3 pF floor the true figure is |G|=0.00903 = 0.90 %, RL 40.88 dB - and the run's own bench agrees (tuning_authority measures s_l0 = -40.8861). Off by 2.25x against its own simulation. Harmless numerically (still 15 dB inside spec).

Acceptance criterion 13 not met by the delivered BOM: the criterion requires each line 'in stock at LCSC or DigiKey ... verified per line with a stock figure and a date'. fab/BOM.csv has no stock column and no date. The data exists in the parts files (parts/5602.json records '373 in stock', re-confirmed this pass) but was not carried into the deliverable.

Acceptance criterion 7 ('EVERY component on the port node is rated >= 250 V working, verified against its datasheet') is unaddressed for R1. README verifies C1 (250 VDC) and J1 (335 Vrms) and is silent on R1, whose datasheet publishes no max working voltage at all (parts/T50R0-250-12X.json: 'MAX VOLTAGE / MAX CURRENT: ABSENT'). Physical risk is nil - a 250 W / 50 ohm element is designed for 111.8 Vrms at rating and sees 86.6 Vrms here - but a criterion that cannot be satisfied from the datasheet should be stated as such, not skipped.

Two README statements that requirements.md section 2 explicitly mandates are missing. Verbatim: 'No isolation, no protection. An open or shorted port, or drive above 150 W, is outside the design envelope; nothing on the board detects or survives it. README must say so.' It does not. The same section asks for the SMA mating-cycle / hot-connect wear note as 'a usage note for the README'; also absent. (Section 8's F1/F2/F3 hazards and the BeO warning ARE all present and correctly worded in README section 5.)

The 0.032 mm lap gap at README.md:171-173 is false precision. Top copper is derived as '1.6 mm PCB + 35 um copper' = 2.635 mm, but JLC's 1.6 mm is a FINISHED thickness that already includes outer copper and mask, and its tolerance is +/-10% = +/-0.16 mm - five times the quoted gap and enough to make it slightly negative. Harmless in practice (R1's tab is 0.127 mm compliant copper and will flex) but the README quotes an 'ideal flat lap joint' to three decimals with no tolerance statement.

README.md:186-187 offers 'let the J1/C1 end of the board overhang the heatsink edge' as the no-machining alternative to the >=7 mm clearance hole under C1. H3 sits at board-local (2.95, 4.20) - inside that end. Overhanging leaves only H1 and H2, both at y=13.8, i.e. two screws on a single line. Needs a half-sentence in the README.

C1's insulated lead must be formed ~3.7 mm outward at assembly and no step says so. The catalogue lead exits ~2.29 mm off the case axis (parts/5602.json note [4]); the footprint places pad 2 at 6.00 mm pitch, which is correct and clearance-driven (5.4 mm would be the 0.80 mm HV minimum). Lead LENGTH is unpublished by Johanson/Knowles. R1's tab carries a 'measure the actual lead at incoming inspection' step; C1's lead has no equivalent.

The 4th verify_all warning (constraints_drift) is unwaived and unexplained. Diffed both files: the only substantive difference is that kicad/constraints.json carries planes[0..1].connect = 'solid' (decision 57) and architecture/constraints.json does not; everything else is a comment key. Checks ran against the as-built copy, so this is source-of-truth drift only. Syncing the architecture copy clears the warning. Same class of drift: architecture/blocks.md still describes a 24.0 x 16.0 mm outline and +/-4.75 mm strap lands against an as-built 26.0 x 20.0 and +/-5.10.

clean: C1 case (pad 1, 7.6 mm annulus / 6.3 mm plated hole) is on GND and the insulated lead is /RF - the metal an operator touches is at ground potential, as requirements s8 F1 demands. Verified from the board, not the decision log.
R1's two GND strap lands exist, are on GND, are 100% contained in the F.Cu pour, have stitching vias touching them (0.000 mm), carry F.Mask + F.Paste, and clear the RF lap pad by 0.85 mm.
J1 barrel projects 7.70 mm clear of the north board edge; a mated SMA nut reaches x=39.14 against C1's body envelope starting at x=42.39 - 3.25 mm of clearance.
C1 top-adjust access with cable mated and board bolted down: criterion 6 satisfied.
Heatsink clearance hole under C1 (>=7 mm dia) fits the placement: spans board-local 18.35-25.35 x 0.80-7.80 inside the 26 x 20 outline.
Outline is exactly 26.0 x 20.0 mm (criterion 10, 30x30 HARD, met at 43% of area).
Thermal chain fully reproduced: 120 C flange at 150 W, Rth <= 0.633 C/W, 0.212 C/W grease on 2.359 cm2, heatsink <= 0.421 C/W, Wakefield 168.5 W / 116 C, Fischer 85.5 W / 133 C.
DFM: 1 warning, 6 silk strokes at 0.12 mm, all six from J1's stock footprint graphics; README s7 documents it accurately.
All five blocks.md open items (OPEN-1..5) are closed in the delivered artifacts.
The metal-shim -> insulating-shim reversal is explicitly recorded as a consequence of adopting architecture B3, not an accident.
